graph.label: Living map of the base: facts, stories, open questions, and gaps marked [CONFIRM].

story.title: It grounds your business, then the tree knows it.
story.lead1: SkillTree interviews and skills are one layer. Agent KBase is the company knowledge base those agents read: offers, constraints, voice, and what must stay [CONFIRM].
story.lead2: That is the difference between an AI org that shares ground truth and a folder of generic prompts.
story.priceExample: Price gap. The site said the price was on request. The draft wrote from €99. In the notes that line stays: Price: [CONFIRM]. The 99 is not published.
story.proofEmpty: Empty, until a real client agrees to be named.
story.visualDraftText: Thank you, Ana. From the folder: what you sell and who it is for.
story.visualLowText: One star. I want a refund.
story.visualSuggestText: Thank you, Luis. I will reply myself.
story.step1Body: Every agent that speaks for the business starts from brain/. Offers, constraints, voice, and what must stay [CONFIRM].
story.step2Body: Facts, stories, and open questions are files. The wizard and the CLI write the same pack. Git is how you change it.
story.step3Title: Validate and eval are the observe loop
story.step3Body: brain validate checks the folder. brain eval checks a draft for a price that is not in the facts. Neither one publishes.
story.step4Title: The wizard is how you start
story.step4Body: Paste the public site, correct the draft, and export brain.zip. Nothing goes live until you say yes.
story.faqMcpQ: Is the MCP a write API?
story.faqMcpA: No. brain_brief, brain_search, brain_read, brain_list, brain_open_questions, brain_validate, and brain_eval are read-only.
story.faqGitA: In git. The wizard and the CLI export the same pack. The MCP server does not create, edit, or delete facts.
story.faqLiveA: After you say yes. A price, a client, or a claim that is not in the folder is cut or marked [CONFIRM].
story.extractTitle: Point at your site and add the facts. The brain comes out in a structure agents understand.
story.extractLead: Step 1 of the wizard: paste a public URL. We read titles, headings, and body copy, then draft mission text, fact bullets, and story beats onto the map. Open questions land on GAPS as [CONFIRM] until you approve them.
story.extractMuted: The graph is the same radial layout teams use for audits: scan the public page, plan on spokes, export only after you edit. SkillTree runs paid full stack audits; Agent KBase gives you the OSS map and zip for your repo.
story.synced: Nodes synced from your wizard draft
story.sample: Sample after URL extract · FACTS and GAPS highlighted ·

company.title: Notes on what you sell. The drafts come from there.
company.lead: Paste your site. Edit the draft until you recognize the offer, the client, and what must not be said. The program that writes the article and the one that writes the post both read those notes. You say yes before anything is published.
company.stepsTitle: From your site to a draft you recognize
company.step1: Paste the public URL and get a draft.
company.step2: Cross out any service, price, or deadline you do not sell.
company.step3: Write who you serve, and what you will not claim.
company.step4: Ask a client question. The answer can use only the notes.
company.step5: If the draft sounds like you, an article can follow. The LinkedIn post waits until the article is published. Both wait for your yes.
company.checksLead: If one fails, the draft stays put.
company.check1: The title is a problem in your business, in words you would use.
company.check2: Every price, pack, or deadline is in your notes. If it is missing, it is cut.
company.check3: A ranking, a visit count, or a client gets in only if you can open it on a page.
company.check4: Each fact shows where it came from: your site, your service list, or your notes.
company.check5: The close asks them to write. No invoices, no passwords, and no personal mobile.
company.firstArticle: The first piece that used this list:
company.articleTitle: How to stop my blog posting a price I do not charge
company.core1: The draft arrives on WhatsApp. You approve it or you stop it.
company.core2: The article goes on the site only with that yes.
company.core3: The LinkedIn post comes from an article that is already published.
company.price: The open folder is free. Setup, the start call, and the written agreement are quoted. [CONFIRM: fee or range.]
company.connectors: Connectors that would publish on their own, after the yes, are still in preparation. This page does not open that list.

wizard.title: A draft from your site
wizard.lead: Paste the public address of your page. We read titles, headings, and text. You get a draft: what you sell, who it is for, and what stays [CONFIRM]. It is a reading of your page. It is not a new offer. An agent is the program that will draft from these notes later. This step only prepares the draft. You correct it. Nothing is published here.

check.lead: Paste LinkedIn copy, an email, or an article. We run the same five checks against your company sheet. Green means no invented price against your facts — you still say yes before anything goes live.
